subject: Temporary hosted SLO guardrail amendment request
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@fincorp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLO guardrail amendment for scheduled migration

Vanessa,

We’re planning a multi-stage data migration the week of Nov 8–12 that will shift a subset of real-time traffic through a new ingestion tier. The migration plan (attached) shows a 3-hour maintenance window on the 9th where we expect transient request fan-out and a spike in tail latency.

Our concerns: if p95 is measured across a tight epoch during the spike we’ll trigger a breach and downstream pager noise. We’d like to request a short-term SLO amendment for the hosted API: either a targeted carveout for the migration window (Nov 9, 03:00–06:00 UTC) or a temporary relaxation of the p95 measurement window for that day. We expect the traffic shape to return to normal after the migration.

As background: FinCorp is in the last phase of a major customer migration and needs assurance that a single scheduled event won’t count as a formal SLA breach. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood would need to approve a temporary carveout (logs, KV-cache snapshots, routing decisions)? Also include any options for a burst-capacity add-on and whether credits would be applied for the impacted period.

Thanks,
Sarah Lewis
Head of Platform Operations | FinCorp
Attachment: migration-plan.pdf (12 pages)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-18T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary SLO guardrail amendment for scheduled migration

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding a customer request from FinCorp. Two asks from them: a carveout for a narrow maintenance window OR a temporary measurement-window relaxation for Nov 9.

Quick thoughts:
- We can offer a 6-hour carveout (02:00–08:00 UTC) scoped to a single route with explicit start/end times and a documented evidence package.
- Alternatively, a 24-hour measurement-epoch extension (aggregate p95 across 24 hours) is riskier for other customers but could be scoped to their account id and agreed in the contract addendum.
- We should attach a short remediation plan: automated fallback to a cheaper variant/model and temporary routed burst capacity from Dedicated pools to reduce tail risk.

I’ve drafted a short proposal spreadsheet (attached) with pricing scenarios and suggested credits if they take the carveout path. Karthik — can you confirm whether the Dedicated burst is feasible on those dates? Marissa — I need a short legal-friendly sentence we can send them about auditability (what logs we’ll provide) and the DocuSign cadence.

Vanessa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Attachment: temp_slo_proposal.xlsx (3 sheets)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary SLO guardrail amendment for scheduled migration

Vanessa —

Technical approval from my side with two provisos:
1) Keep p50/p95 targets unchanged for contractual language; implement the carveout as an "operational exception" that is explicitly timeboxed and annotated in our SLO measurement pipeline. We should store a signed amendment and annotate the measurement epoch so the automated SLO calculator excludes that window for FinCorp.
2) Provide a minimal evidence bundle: routing decision logs (route_id + timestamp), per-request latency samples (hashed request id), and a short post-mortem within 72 hours. That’s sufficient for audit and keeps our telemetry chain intact.

Operational notes:
- Karthik, can we guarantee the requested Dedicated pool burst on Nov 9 + contingency if we see >20% additional p95 pressure? If not, we should propose a scaled fallback: conditional routing to a compatible smaller model + crediting the customer for any measurable degradation.

I’ll draft the amendment text. We should aim for a one-paragraph legal note and one technical appendix.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@fincorp.com>, Ops Team <ops@fincorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO guardrail amendment for scheduled migration

Sarah — thanks for the clear heads-up and the migration plan. We can accommodate a timeboxed operational carveout with the following proposal attached: "Redwood Temporary SLO Amendment v1". Key points here in plain language: 

1) Scope: carveout applies to FinCorp account only and to the hosted inference route ids listed in your migration plan.
2) Window: Nov 9, 02:00–08:00 UTC (we expanded by 1 hour on either side to cover rollbacks).
3) Measurement: automated SLO measurement will exclude requests that match the route + account id within that window; p50/p95 contractual thresholds remain unchanged outside the carveout.
4) Evidence: we will provide routing decision logs, anonymized per-request latency samples, and a 72-hour post-event summary.
4a) For auditability we will provide a signed appendix and a verification CSV.
5) Operational mitigations: we will activate a Dedicated burst capacity for that window and preconfigure fallback routing to a compatible quantized model if p95 crosses a defined threshold.
6) Credits: If we fail to deliver the mitigation plan and a breach occurs attributable to Redwood routing, we propose a one-time credit equal to one week of average monthly usage for the affected routes (details in attached PDF).

Next steps — please review the attached amendment and confirm acceptance by Oct 22 so we can lock capacity and draft the DocuSign. If you prefer the alternative (24-hour epoch extension), we can outline that as option B but we recommend the timeboxed carveout as narrower and easier to audit.

Attachment: redwood-temp-slo-amendment-v1.pdf (5 pages)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
